function.name: read_component
function.description: Read one Lattice component (layout): its authoring skeleton, slot contracts, word budget, variant decision rule, when to use it and its anti-patterns. The variant examples and the rest are listed by section; call again with `section` for one.

name.description: The component name, e.g. kpi, cards-grid.

section.description: Optional: one section of the doc, e.g. Variants, Anatomy.

function.name: read_front_matter
function.description: Read how a front-matter key works: its values, defaults and what it changes.

key.description: The key, e.g. finish, mode, theme, venue.

function.name: read_guide
function.description: Read a Lattice authoring guide. Topics: accessibility-review, chart-from-data, deck, diagram, edit-deck, finish, fix-findings, lens, math, restyle-deck, speaker-notes, studio, theme, editorial, principles, universals. Long guides return a section list; call again with `section`.

section.description: Optional: a section heading (or part of one).

function.name: read_slides
function.description: Read the exact Markdown of slides from the current draft (including your edits this turn).

function.name: preview_speech
function.description: Show what the voice will say aloud, before you guess a pronunciation. For slides (`from`, optional `to`, up to 10 at a time) it reads each slide the way Present and the export do: its spoken line (say:) first, then a front-matter say: entry, then chart narration, then the slide text. It names which one it read, lists each deck term that fired as written → as spoken (a possessive or plural is listed on its own), and lists words no term covers that a voice may stumble on (all-caps runs, a dot inside a word, odd capitals; names from other languages are not detected). Speaker notes are never read aloud. Or pass `text` to hear any words, for example a term before you add it with set_terms.

text.description: Any words to hear instead of slides.

function.name: find_text
function.description: Find words across the draft without reading every slide. Returns each match with its slide, the field it is in (heading, eyebrow, body, quote, alt text, spoken line, note, description, code, math, html, record) and the words around it, plus matches in the front matter, listed apart. Search for the words a reader sees: `$5` finds an escaped `\$5`, and `Oct` is found inside bold or a link. Literal text, not a pattern. Use it before replace_text, and instead of read_slides when you are looking for a term.

text.description: The words to find, up to 200 characters.

whole_word.description: Match whole words only. Default false.

function.name: check_deck
function.description: Run Lattice's linter and review over the draft, and Mermaid's parser over its diagrams. Returns the errors and warnings with slide numbers, and slides over the word budget.

function.name: list_assets
function.description: Search the Library photos and videos the author added. The prompt lists the newest; use this to find others by name, caption, shape (portrait, landscape, square, panorama) or kind. Returns name, shape, pixel size, scope and caption.

query.description: Words to match against name, caption and shape.

function.name: view_asset
function.description: Look at up to 6 Library photos you need to choose by what they show. A photo that already has a caption comes back as its caption, not as a picture. Pictures arrive in the next message; then call caption_asset for each so you never look at it again. Do not look at photos you can pick by name and shape.

again.description: Look at a captioned photo anyway, for example to correct its caption.

function.name: render_slide
function.description: Look at one slide of the draft, rendered the way export draws it. The picture arrives in the next message. Use it to judge a layout you are unsure of, not on every slide; at most 3 per turn.

function.name: edit_slides
function.description: Stage slide edits on the draft. replace: `body` is the WHOLE new slide (its `<!-- _class -->` line through its last line), exactly one slide. insert: new slide(s) after slide `slide` (0 = before the first); separate several with a line containing only `---`. delete: removes slide `slide`. Edits apply in order; numbers refer to the draft as it stands. The result includes the checker’s verdict on the draft.

summary.description: One or two sentences to the author: what you changed and why. If the checker finds no errors this is your whole answer for the turn.

function.name: set_front_matter
function.description: Stage a front-matter change on the draft: set a scalar key, or remove it with value null. Read the key first. The result includes the checker’s verdict on the draft.

summary.description: One or two sentences to the author: what you changed and why. If the checker finds no errors this is your whole answer for the turn.

function.name: set_terms
function.description: Stage changes to how the deck’s words are spoken (the `terms:` front matter; it also absorbs `acronyms:` and `lexicon:`). Each `set` entry adds or replaces one term: `pronounce` is how the voice says it (empty string silences it), `expansion` what it stands for, `definition` a glossary line. One entry also covers the plural, possessive, hyphenated and title-case forms, so never add those separately. The slides keep the word as written. Call preview_speech first to hear how a line reads now.

pronounce.description: How to say it; "" silences the term; null clears it so the voice says the expansion.

summary.description: One or two sentences to the author: what you changed and why.

function.name: replace_text
function.description: Stage a find-and-replace across the draft: every match in headings, eyebrows, body, quotes, alt text, spoken lines, notes and descriptions. It works the way a word processor does: the words change and their formatting stays (replace `Oct` in **Oct** and it stays bold). Write the replacement as plain words; characters Markdown would read as markup (`$`, `*`, `[`…) are escaped for you, so `$5` shows as $5. It never touches link or image targets, URLs, directives, code blocks, math, HTML, `{…}` records or the front matter; a match that crosses formatting (`**Oct.** Tenth`) is left alone; it reports what it left alone (for terms in the front matter use set_terms). Literal text, not a pattern; with case_sensitive false the replacement is written exactly as given. For a word or phrase change use this, not edit_slides: you send only the words, and the author reviews one card. The result includes the checker’s verdict on the draft.

find.description: The words to replace, up to 200 characters.

replace.description: What to write instead. One line; may be empty to delete the words.

whole_word.description: Match whole words only. Default false.

slides.description: Only these slides. Default: every slide.

summary.description: One or two sentences to the author: what you changed and why. If the checker finds no errors this is your whole answer for the turn.

function.name: set_theme
function.description: Change the deck's theme (its palette) on the draft. Same as setting the `theme:` front-matter key.

function.name: set_finish
function.description: Change the deck's finish (the backdrop behind every slide) on the draft; "none" removes it. Same as setting `finish:`. read_guide finish first if unsure.

function.name: chart_from_data
function.description: Put numbers on a NEW slide as a chart, on the draft. bar compares categories; line shows a trend over ordered steps; piechart shows parts of one whole (values summing to 100%); stacked-bar shows what each total is made of (give `parts`). Write the heading as the claim the numbers make. Values keep their units: `$4.2M`, `68%`, `12,400`. Read the chart guide (read_component) if unsure.

after.description: Insert after this slide number (0 puts it first).

variant.description: Optional: bar row (long names) or diverging (signed values); piechart donut.

function.name: create_deck
function.description: Create a NEW deck from complete Lattice Markdown (front matter, then slides separated by ---), for when the author asks for a new deck rather than a change to this one. It does not happen yet: the author sees the title and outline and confirms. Call it once per turn, after drafting the whole deck; then tell the author it is ready for them to confirm. The open deck is not changed.

markdown.description: The whole deck in Lattice Markdown.

function.name: caption_asset
function.description: Save a one-line description of each photo you just looked at (under 20 words, plain, what is in the picture: subject, setting, light, any visible text). It is stored with the photo and read as text from now on.
